title: Kempf vanishing for dominant flag line bundles
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Let $\lambda\in X$ satisfy $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$. Extend $\lambda$ to $\widetilde\lambda=\lambda\circ(B\to T)$ and let $Q=S/B$. Let $\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda}$ be the homogeneous invertible sheaf of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], defined by the right action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\lambda(b)z)$ on $S\times\mathbf A^1$. Write $H^i(Q,-)=R^i\Gamma(Q,-)$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology, computed by an injective resolution of sheaves of $\mathcal O_Q$-modules. Then
$$H^i(Q,\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda})=0\qquad\text{for every integer }i>0.$$
This holds in every characteristic, including for an empty root system.

source.place: Section 22d, pp.479--480, Theorems 22.50--22.51, with signs corrected to the line-bundle definition in 18c and 22.48; Jantzen 2003 II.4.5 and II.5.10--5.12 are WANTED.

proof.text:
For every character $\mu$ write $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\mu}$. The homogeneous-line-bundle statement supplies these actual invertible coherent modules and their trivializations on $S$. The multiplication map of trivial lines sends $(z,w)$ to $zw$: under $b\in B$ its factor is $\widetilde\mu(b)\widetilde
u(b)=\widetilde{\mu+
u}(b)$. The fpqc descent equivalence therefore gives $M_\mu\otimes M_
u\simeq M_{\mu+
u}$ and $M_0\simeq\mathcal O_Q$, compatibly with these trivializations. Consequently $M_\mu^{\otimes a}\simeq M_{a\mu}$ for $a\ge0$, and $M_\mu^{-1}\simeq M_{-\mu}$. These are sheaf identities, not just equalities of global sections.

source.place: 18c, pp.389--390, tensoring the specified descent data; 22.48, p.479.

proof.text: The regular-dominant ampleness statement makes $Q$ smooth projective geometrically integral. The Borel-pair statement also gives properness. By the rho-pairing statement, $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$ for each simple root. Since $\lambda$ is dominant, both $\lambda+\rho$ and $\lambda+2\rho$ have strictly positive simple-coroot pairings, even if some pairings of $\lambda$ vanish. Hence $A=M_{\lambda+\rho}$ and $A'=M_{\lambda+2\rho}$ are ample. These applications include the empty root system by the explicit rank-zero clause of the ampleness node.

source.place: 22.49--22.51, p.480; regular-dominant geometric inputs made explicit.

proof.text: Suppose first that $\operatorname{char}F=p_0>0$. By properness and the proper-field coherence statement, $Q$ is Noetherian and $M_{-\rho}$ is coherent. Apply Serre vanishing to this module and the ample invertible module $A=M_{\lambda+\rho}$. Choose $n_0$ so that $H^i(Q,M_{-\rho}\otimes A^{\otimes n})=0$ for all $n\ge n_0$ and $i>0$. Choose $r\ge1$ with $q=p_0^r\ge n_0$; this is possible since $p_0\ge2$. Step 1 identifies the vanishing module at $n=q$ with $M_{q(\lambda+\rho)-\rho}=M_{q\lambda+(q-1)\rho}$.

source.place: II.4.5, local book WANTED; explicit Serre twisting assembly in the Andersen–Haboush argument cited by Milne 22.51.

proof.text:
Let $f=f_r=\operatorname{Fr}_Q^r$ and $D=M_{(q-1)\rho}$. The Andersen–Haboush input gives finiteness of $f$ and $f_*D\simeq\mathcal O_Q^{\oplus d_r}$ with $d_r\ge1$. In a Zariski frame of $M_\lambda$, pullback by $f$ raises every transition unit $u_{ab}$ to $u_{ab}^{q}$. These are exactly the transition units of $M_\lambda^{\otimes q}$, so $f^*M_\lambda\simeq M_{q\lambda}$ by step 1. Apply the finite ideal-twist cohomology comparison with $Y=X=Q$, its coherent module $\mathcal F=D$, ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal O_Q$, invertible module $\mathcal L=M_\lambda$ and exponent $n=1$. Its local-Noetherian hypotheses hold by step 3, and $D$ is coherent by the homogeneous-line-bundle statement. It gives
$$H^i(Q,f_*D\otimes M_\lambda)\simeq H^i(Q,D\otimes f^*M_\lambda)=H^i(Q,M_{q\lambda+(q-1)\rho})=0\quad(i>0).$$
Here the last equality is step 3; no ampleness of $M_\lambda$ was assumed.

source.place: II.4.4--4.5, local book WANTED; sheaf pushforward formula and projection/cohomology assembly. Stacks coherent.tex Tags 0B5V (lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample), 01YP (lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal), 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology), and cohomology.tex Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula), as recorded by the cited finite comparison.

proof.text: The sheaf isomorphism $f_*D\simeq\mathcal O_Q^{\oplus d_r}$ identifies $f_*D\otimes M_\lambda$ with $M_\lambda^{\oplus d_r}$. Since $d_r\ge1$, injection into its first summand and projection out of it compose to $\mathrm{id}_{M_\lambda}$. Applying the cohomology functor preserves this composite, so $H^i(Q,M_\lambda)$ is a retract of the zero group in step 4, and is zero. This proves the positive-characteristic case, including $p_0=2$, $\lambda=0$ and empty roots.

source.place: II.4.5, local book WANTED; elementary retract argument concluding the positive-characteristic proof.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}F=0$, the canonical-character statement gives $\omega_Q\simeq M_{-2\rho}$. With $A'=M_{\lambda+2\rho}$ from step 2, step 1 gives $\omega_Q\otimes A'\simeq M_\lambda$. The flag scheme satisfies all the Kodaira hypotheses: smooth, projective and geometrically integral by step 2, pure dimension $|\Phi^+|$ by the canonical-character statement, over the given algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, with $A'$ ample. Kodaira vanishing therefore gives $H^i(Q,M_\lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$. Its dimension-zero case includes the empty root system. A field has characteristic zero or prime positive characteristic, so these two cases exhaust the statement.
